newsitem.title: NORWAY: Partners mull new gas line linking Troll platforms.
newsitem.headline: Partners mull new gas line linking Troll platforms.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday partners in the Troll development were looking at plans for a gas pipeline linking the Troll C oil platform to the Troll A gas installation.

The 30-km line would pipe associated gas from Troll C oil production to Troll A, where it would be blended with other production and transported onshore at Kollsnes near Bergen on the west coast for treatment and export.

Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter said improved recovery from the oil-bearing layers in the Troll West gas province would yield a steady output of 10 million cubic metres per day of gas over 15 years of expected oil production.

Transporting the extra gas would require expanded capacity in the lines from Troll A to Kollsnes, Statoil said. Four compressors are due to be installed on the platform by 2007, with two possibly arriving in 1999.
"Increasing starting pressure in the lines from 60 to 90 bar would boost throughput from 84 to 100 million cubic metres per day without needing additional equipment," Statoil said.

Troll Oil operator Norsk Hydro will submit a plan for the installation and operation of the new pipeline from C to A in October. Statoil will study export solutions for the associated gas, Status Weeekly said.
